title: wmti walks itself
description: A guided tour of the wmti viewer's own architecture: a pure core wrapped in a thin Neovim shell. Read top to bottom to see how a :WmtiOpen turns a JSON file into a stepped, drift-tolerant tour.

steps.title: Commands are the only entry point
steps.why: The plugin ships no default keymaps — it exposes itself purely through :Wmti* commands so it never clobbers your bindings. Each command thunks into require('wmti'), which is what lets lazy.nvim defer loading until you actually run one.

steps.title: Open flow: notify, auto, or pick
steps.why: The open decision lives here, not in the UI: zero walkthroughs notify, exactly one auto-opens (no wasted keystroke), many fall through to the picker. :WmtiSelect reuses select() to always re-prompt.

steps.title: The filesystem boundary
steps.why: All disk access for walkthroughs is funneled through this module: glob .wmti/*.json, read bytes, hand the string to core.load. Keeping I/O here is what lets core stay pure and testable without touching a real file.

steps.title: The heart: drift-tolerant resolve
steps.why: This is why the viewer survives code moving after authoring. It matches the step's anchor text against the current buffer (exact, then whitespace-trimmed), picks the occurrence nearest the recorded line, and re-spans — falling back to the raw line with a 'moved' flag when the anchor is gone. Pure function, no Neovim.

steps.title: Wiring core into windows
steps.why: goto_step is the seam between pure logic and the editor: it loads the file into the code window, feeds its lines to core.resolve, then centers and highlights the result — and deliberately returns focus to the sidebar so you can keep stepping (sidebar-driven preview).

steps.title: What you actually read
steps.why: The sidebar shows every step's title but the full 'why' for the current step only, plus its resolved location and any 'may have moved' / 'file missing' flag. Re-rendering from scratch each step keeps the panel a dumb projection of session state.

steps.anchor: h.test("resolve relocates to the exact anchor when lines have drifted", function()
steps.title: Proof the drift handling works
steps.why: core is the single tested seam. This spec injects a lines table where the anchored code has shifted down and asserts resolve relocates to it — exercising the exact behavior step 4 promises, with zero Neovim, git, or real files involved.
